hits.name: Alex Finn

I've been using Claude Duet the last couple hours and I'll say this:

It's EXCELLENT

The multi tasking is probably the best in the space

You get one simple thread you can talk to, and as you give it commands and prompts, it automatically spins up tasks on a list for you

So instead of having to manage a ton of side chats that could get long or confusing, you have 1 chat, but it makes 'task' threads automatically that you can watch and monitor

This allows you to just keep brain dumping ideas and tasks into the one thread, and not have to worry about the agent getting confused. The agent just will manage all the tasks for you

Very similar to Claude Code's new 'projects' feature which was probably a beta test for this

The coding was great. Built me a bunch of PRs quickly I was able to review. 

Proactivity was fantastic too. Came up with a bunch of tasks on its own and just asked me for the go ahead

As expected it's also fantastic to talk to. Claude has long been the best model to converse with (outside Opus 5) and the carries over to Claude Duet

Really pleased with the product, even in research preview. Very excited to see where it goes from here

Definitely sign up for the wait list

hits.name: GREG ISENBERG
hits.text:
Yes, 99.9% of Duo apps look like trash now but what did you expect? 

Most companies won’t redesign for a new device until it has millions of users, so the first year is always a little messy.

So, startup idea for you coming from someone who has sold tens of millions of dollars of agency services: a Duo app agency.

Think about who’s buying this thing! Someone paying $2000+ for a phone the week it comes out is about as valuable a customer as you’ll find on the App Store. 

They pay for apps, they pay for subscriptions, and they leave reviews. Most companies want those people badly, and most don’t have a spare team to redesign their app for a brand new screen. Hence, why the Duo apps look mostly trash now.

How to start a duo app agency:

Pick the categories where the bigger screen matters, like recipes, reading, trading, design and music. Record a short video of their app looking cramped on the Duo next to an AI mockup of what it could look like. Charge $40k to $75k to ship the redesign in a few weeks, and a monthly retainer to keep it right as Apple updates things.

One of the most obvious startup ideas out there right now. I’d start this today.

Sometimes the best startup ideas are the most obvious!

His play: pick categories where the big screen matters, record the app looking cramped next to a mockup of what it could be, and pitch the redesign. Those are his price numbers, not proven ones.

outsiders.name: MartyParty
outsiders.text:
The attack vector today is to steal AI API keys. 

These are keys that allow agents to query the LLM. By stealing them the attacker can use AI for free and the API key owner is charged on their credit card. 

AI API keys function as bearer tokens for metered, prepaid compute: whoever holds a valid key can generate tokens, and the bill lands on the account owner. There is no mining or blockchain involved just unauthorized inference that the key holder pays for.

This has nothing to do with crypto. This is an attack on prepaid client side AI.

virals.draft_en:
Two days, three security stories: a critical PHP bug, a Node patch, and the Railway hack.

Most of the people you love will never read a security thread. Send them this:

1. Use a password manager, never reuse passwords
2. Two-factor auth with an app or security key, not SMS
3. Auto-updates on, restart weekly
4. Freeze your credit
5. Ask your carrier for a port-out PIN

Takes an evening. Saves a lot of pain.
virals.inspired_by: @mckaywrigley educate your family (426k) + @peterwildeford PSA list (593k) + @tdinh_me 2 days of vulns (6.6k)
virals.video_tip: 12s: a family group chat, the five steps dropping in one at a time, caption send this to your parents.

virals.angle: Your AI API key is a credit card
virals.draft_en:
Railway disclosed a breach that may have exposed customer environment variables, including API keys.

An AI API key is basically a credit card for compute. Whoever has it can run models and you get the bill.

Tonight:
1. Rotate every key
2. Set a hard monthly spend limit in each AI dashboard
3. One key per agent or app
4. Turn on usage alerts

Ten minutes. Do it before you need to.

virals.video_tip: 10s: a credit card with 'API KEY' printed on it, a spend meter shooting up, then capped, caption set the limit.

virals.angle: The personal agent race, user's version
virals.draft_en:
Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive agent that comes to you with what needs attention and checks with you before acting.

That makes four big personal agents now. Alex Finn thinks this race matters more than the model race, because people hand these agents their email, calendar and finances.

Before you pick one, ask three things:
1. What can it do without asking me?
2. Can I see what it did?
3. Can I revoke access in one click?

virals.draft_en:
After the PHP scare, some people said it's the end of PHP. Pieter disagrees: AI-assisted bug finding will hit every language and framework, and Node patched a serious bug the same week.

The teams that did well this week weren't on a safer stack. They knew what they ran, patched fast, and rotated keys.

Theo said his agents triaged the outages and rolled dozens of keys for him. That's the use worth setting up now.

virals_narrative: Window Oct 22 ~11:15 CT (after Wednesday's digest) through Oct 22 ~11:15 CT. Security stayed the story. A day after the PHP patch, Railway disclosed a breach that may have exposed customer environment variables, including API keys, and paused deployments (314k for the first report). Greg Isenberg framed AI keys as credit cards for compute and posted a 10 minute fix (97k), and Theo spent hours stuck without deploys. The most useful post was a checklist: McKay Wrigley told people to walk their families through Peter Wildeford's PSA on password managers, app-based 2FA, credit freezes and carrier PINs (426k, 2.3k bookmarks). Pieter brought his sites back after the PHP fix (107k) and argued AI-assisted bug finding will hit every stack, not just PHP (53k). On the product side, Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive personal agent (7.9M), and Alex Finn called the personal agent race more important than the model race (177k). Pieter's off-lane European politics posts drew big numbers (159k) but aren't drafted. The meta: on scary news days, a short checklist people can forward wins; post the prompt after the demo; and when a new device or agent lands, explain what it means for regular users.
